scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You catch an infection and your temperature shoots up. Is fever the illness, or is your body doing it on purpose?

scenes.name: thermostat
scenes.text: A part of your brain called the hypothalamus works like a thermostat, keeping you near thirty seven degrees.

scenes.name: signals
scenes.text: When immune cells detect germs, they release chemical signals that travel to the brain.

scenes.name: reset
scenes.text: These signals raise the thermostat's set point. Now your normal temperature feels too cold.

scenes.name: chills
scenes.text: So you shiver and get chills, and blood vessels in the skin narrow, to heat you up.

scenes.name: why
scenes.text: A higher temperature can slow some germs, and helps parts of the immune system work faster.

scenes.name: care
scenes.text: Most fevers pass, but a very high or long fever, or one in a baby, needs a doctor. This is general info, not medical advice.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Detect, signal, reset, heat up. Follow for more on how things really work.
